_effort_note: Reasoning level is set by the CLI's --variant flag (provider-specific reasoning effort), NOT by a DSH overlay. max is passed explicitly.

_notes.surface: OpenCode CLI one-shot agent run (opencode run); a real agent loop with file read/write and shell, not a chat completion
_notes.why_cli: opencode/ll-alpha-free is a free stealth model that the OpenCode service refuses over plain HTTP: /zen/v1 and /inference/v1 answer 403 FreeTierError ('free tier can only be used from within OpenCode'), and /zen/go/v1 does not carry it. Verified 2026-10-17: ll-alpha-free is absent from the 37 ids on /zen/go/v1/models. The CLI is the only working path, so this adapter does NOT use a DSH patch overlay.
_notes.binary: opencode.exe 1.19.3, resolved as the package bin of opencode-ai (the .cmd wrapper just forwards to it); called directly so subprocess needs no shell
_notes.fresh_session: each invocation mints a new sessionID (no -c/-s passed), which is what the benchmark requires
_notes.prompt: the two-line dispatch text is passed verbatim as one argv element; cli_suite starts the process with cwd set to the external run workdir
_notes.auto: --auto auto-approves permissions so the headless run can write files; the sandbox boundary is still the host filesystem, so isolation stays unverified per protocol 2.0
_notes.evidence: --format json emits newline-delimited events (step_start / tool_use / text / step_finish) to stdout, which cli_suite stores in stdout.log; step_finish carries token usage and cost, so usage IS recoverable for this adapter (unlike the DSH adapters)
_notes.identity: the requested model is a CLI declaration; the trace records sessionID and per-step usage but does not independently attest the upstream model id
